issues.summary: The skew-tolerated notBefore/expirationTime are copied into JWT nbf/exp, and jwt.verify has no clockTolerance. /v1/auth/verify then throws a non-HTTP error, returning 500 after the nonce is spent and the user is created.
issues.label: medium
issues.evidence: auth.service.ts:82-92 copies notBefore/expirationTime into nbf/exp. auth.controller.ts:136,205 calls getTokenPayloadWithClaims → decodeToken → jwt.verify (jwt.module.ts:58-66, no clockTolerance), which throws NotBeforeError/TokenExpiredError. global-error.filter.ts:29-35 maps non-HttpExceptions to 500, and siwe.repository.ts clears the nonce before this point. The login would have failed before the PR too, now with a clean 401, so this is mainly a worse failure mode plus a notBefore case the fix doesn't solve. An iat in the future (F25) is not checked by jsonwebtoken without maxAge.

issues.summary: No endpoint/integration test covers a message accepted within the skew window all the way through AuthService and token issuance.
issues.label: medium
issues.evidence: The only integration change (auth.controller.integration.spec.ts ~398-407) tests rejection beyond the window, and siwe-message.entity.spec.ts only exercises the schema. An end-to-end test would have caught the nbf/exp 500 above.

issues.summary: AUTH.md says the skew allowance avoids rejecting valid messages, but within-skew notBefore/expirationTime still fail downstream.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: AUTH.md:235 claims this. Because of the JWT nbf/exp verification failure, it only holds for issuedAt.

issues.summary: AUTH_CLOCK_SKEW_SECONDS has no entry in the configuration schema, so negative, huge or non-numeric values are not rejected at startup.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: configuration.schema.ts:63 validates AUTH_STATE_TTL_MILLISECONDS with .int().min(1) but has no AUTH_CLOCK_SKEW_SECONDS entry, and configuration.ts:52-55 parses it unchecked. A negative value makes the check `issuedAt > now + skewMs` reject fresh messages, and a huge value disables the expiry/notBefore checks. Both require operator misconfiguration.

issues.summary: A NaN skew (non-numeric env) is silently treated as 0 by the truthiness check instead of surfacing an error.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: siwe-message.entity.ts:59 `clockSkewSeconds ? clockSkewSeconds * 1_000 : 0` turns NaN into 0. This falls back safely to the pre-PR strict behaviour, but a misconfiguration goes unnoticed.

issues.summary: clockSkewSeconds is optional with a no-skew branch, although the only caller always passes a number.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: siwe.repository.ts reads it with getOrThrow<number> and always passes it to buildSiweMessageSchema (siwe-message.entity.ts:30). The optional parameter costs nothing concrete beyond a style or readability point.

issues.summary: The Zod schema is rebuilt on every getValidatedSiweMessage call instead of once in the constructor.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: siwe.repository.ts:45 calls buildSiweMessageSchema(this.clockSkewSeconds) per call. Building a small Zod schema once per login is negligible, and caching it would be a style improvement only.

issues.summary: No configuration validator test for AUTH_CLOCK_SKEW_SECONDS.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: src/config/configuration.validator.spec.ts has no case for it. There is also no schema entry to test (see the missing-validation issue), so the gap is mostly a symptom of that.

issues.summary: The 'Message yet valid' wording should be 'Message not yet valid'.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: siwe-message.entity.ts:81 keeps the pre-existing message text, which tests assert on. Only the wording is affected.

issues.summary: The 'Message yet issued' wording should be 'Message not issued yet'.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: siwe-message.entity.ts:64 is the pre-existing message string, unchanged in meaning. Only the wording is affected.

issues.summary: The new AUTH.md table row is wider than its column and misaligns the Markdown table source.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: AUTH.md:257's description exceeds the 50-char column padding, and `yarn format` is `biome format`, which does not format Markdown. The rendered table is unaffected; only the raw source looks misaligned.
